Expo/React Native iOS + Android client. Pure OAuth API consumer of the web contract.
Design system, tokens, brand-string ledger. Publishes values, not stylesheets.
CI, gates, eval harness, test infrastructure. Owns what 'green' means.
Positioning, gailleur.com marketing surfaces, outbound copy. Every public claim traceable to shipped product.
Acceptance against what was actually asked, and the order work happens in. Authors no feature specs, routes no prompts, decides nothing.
Reads everything, writes only security documents, and can hold a release without asking. Cannot clear a hold — only the human can.
JF's proxy: holds the conversation, turns it into queue entries in his own words, carries stations' questions back to him, reports what the factory is doing. Decides nothing.

rulings.text: Three answers: (1) Currency: UK gets GBP, France and other European countries get EUR. (2) Trial cap behavior: hard stop on AI/LLM features once the $10/month cap is hit — no more AI features until next billing month or the tenant upgrades. (3) Design: loop design in now, from the start, not after web starts building — note Stripe is typically integrated as an iframe within existing UI (not a full redirect).

Cancellation timing: run-to-end-of-current-billing-period (web's recommendation) — access stays at the paid tier until the period the tenant already paid for ends, then reverts to the trial's $10/month cap. No proration refunds. Design builds the cancel-confirmation UI reflecting this wording next, web implements once design delivers.

DECIDE 1: A — honour last-known entitlement offline, unbounded, re-read on every successful reconnect (web+mobile's joint recommendation, adopted as-is). DECIDE 2: B — every tenant gets a fresh 90-day trial from the enforcement-launch date, as the standing rule; this applies to the dogfood households too, not a permanent grandfather. Additional requirement: JF wants the dogfood households to go through the REAL trial-to-paid Stripe flow end to end, not skip it — but at a steep discount via a Stripe discount/coupon code: $1/month or $10/year instead of the real $20/mo or $180/yr. JF's words: 'I guess there will be some charges with Stripe, but I believe it worths the test.' He accepts the small real charges as the cost of testing the actual payment path. Build the checkout to accept/apply a discount code; the Stripe-side coupon creation itself is a JF/ops action in the Stripe dashboard, not a web build task.

DECIDE 3: B, unified across trial-expired and cancelled-lapsed (this SUPERSEDES the earlier cancel-ruling's '/month trial cap' wording, which was ambiguous — B is the actual behavior). JF's words: 'the application continues to function except for all the AI functions from prediction, to ingestion, to interpretation, to chat. On the chat, stating the trial is expired, or you have canceled the subscription, and stating you can subscribe to reactivate your subscription and providing a link to the setting billing page where the use can activate or re-activate their subscription.' So: non-AI app functionality (tasks, ledger, views, everything not AI-driven) keeps working normally for a non-paying tenant, whether trial-expired or cancelled-and-lapsed. All AI-surfaced functions go off: prediction, ingestion, interpretation, chat. The chat surface specifically stays reachable but shows an explanatory state (trial expired / subscription cancelled) plus a link to settings/billing where the tenant can (re)activate.

Explicit ruling: no credit card is required to start the 90-day trial — an account/tenant is created and the trial begins with no Stripe interaction at all. A credit card / Stripe checkout is only requested when the tenant chooses to subscribe: at day 90 to continue past the trial, or on an earlier voluntary upgrade. Abuse-control against this stays whatever the existing account-creation gates already provide (invitation code, demo-passcode restrictions, rate limits) — no card-based friction is added.

The question (raised by web's retraction, task-20260924T022956Z-7726): a pay-at-pickup service invoice with no paid marker, like the Macan invoice ("PAYER CE MONTANT / PAY THIS AMOUNT", Status: Open), is it money already spent or a bill to pay?

B, as put to JF: it is a bill to pay. It becomes a "pay $X" task, and the existing Paid action turns it into the transaction. The extract_entities rubric stays as written (extract-entities.ts L353: "A bill/invoice awaiting payment produces NO transaction"), and the #2082 fixture flips to expect no transaction.

Part of the recommendation JF accepted, chief's wording: "If you pick B, I'd have web confirm this invoice actually produces the pay task today." Verify on the real Macan invoice that the pay task is actually created and that Paid converts it. If it is not created, B leaves JF where he started, and that comes back to him.

JF, verbatim: "Let's go with B for the decide."

The options on the table were A, B' and C (web's response task-20260924T023745Z-7066). Chief reads "B" as B', the only B option offered: plain B was already ruled and shown undeliverable. If JF meant otherwise he will say so.

B', as put to JF: keep the rubric and build the missing path, about 2-3 PRs:
- extract_document records payment_status (paid/due/unknown) on invoice kinds;
- an unpaid ingested invoice creates a one-off "Pay $X to <vendor>" task;
- Paid works on one-off bill tasks and records the transaction without needing an obligation.

seamCaveat: openRequests counts a request no reply correlates to AND whose thread (contextId) carries nothing later from the recipient. Messages sent before contextId existed have only the first test, so they still OVER-report: treat an open request as a prompt to check, never as proof of a dropped ball. Requests older than the horizon are counted as abandoned, not open.
